Phase: Phase 0 — Classes, decisions and the audit floor
Name: Class register: CUI categories held (Basic or Specified), Privacy Act records, retention, impact level and cloud, each with its source

Phase: Phase 0 — Classes, decisions and the audit floor
Name: Inventory: where each class already sits, from content and activity explorer under narrowly granted role groups

Phase: Phase 0 — Classes, decisions and the audit floor
Name: Unified audit on and retained, routed to the log platform; a synthetic audit event found by search within the target time

Phase: Phase 0 — Classes, decisions and the audit floor
Name: Tenant root key for Rights Management
Options (decisions): Microsoft-managed key; bring your own key (BYOK), per Book 12, Chapter 09. Decided before the first encrypting label is published
If late (decisions): Rights Management can't be activated, and no encrypting label can be published

Phase: Phase 0 — Classes, decisions and the audit floor
Name: Gate 0 — Classes decided, audit on
Criteria (gates): Class register with every federal overlay decision and its source; inventory showing where each class sits; unified audit on, retention set and routed to the log platform, with a synthetic event found within the target time; the decision record template in use

Phase: Phase 1 — Labels, defaults and Rights Management
Name: Label taxonomy built in a test tenant: classes to labels, scopes, priority, encryption settings, markings, publishing policies

Phase: Phase 1 — Labels, defaults and Rights Management
Name: Default labels and mandatory labeling for files, email, meetings and containers
Options (decisions): A non-encrypting default per item type, with mandatory labeling and a justification for every downgrade; mandatory labeling with no default
If late (decisions): The pilot policy has no defaults, and ring 1 waits

Phase: Phase 1 — Labels, defaults and Rights Management
Name: Rights Management activated and staged: onboarding limited to the label pilot; super user feature off; two recovery operators named

Phase: Phase 1 — Labels, defaults and Rights Management
Name: Privileged Access Gate 1 — Foundation ready (PIM role settings for every tier)
If late (decisions): Recovery operators can't be made eligible through PIM, so the super user procedure can't be rehearsed

Phase: Phase 1 — Labels, defaults and Rights Management
Name: Super user recovery rehearsed in the test tenant with PIM-eligible operators; decryption-continuity test passed

Phase: Phase 1 — Labels, defaults and Rights Management
Name: Ring 1: label policy and pilot defaults for 25 to 50 users, two weeks; label events and downgrade justifications read; labeled sample passes

Phase: Phase 1 — Labels, defaults and Rights Management
Name: Ring 2: one or two offices per CUI program, two weeks; then the production policy for everyone in scope

Phase: Phase 1 — Labels, defaults and Rights Management
Name: Gate 1 — Labels in use
Criteria (gates): Label policy widened past ring 2 on its recorded criteria; labeled sample file and email with the label in the audit log; defaults set; users outside the policy recorded; super user off with no standing members, recovery rehearsed and the decryption-continuity test passed

Phase: Phase 2 — Containers, SharePoint and OneDrive, and mail
Name: Label integration for SharePoint and OneDrive, legacy IRM libraries, PDFs and co-authoring
Owner or approver: Policy owner, with the records officer
Options (decisions): Integration on before the first encrypting label leaves the pilot; PDFs only after Chapter 09's simulations include them; each IRM library migrated, then IRM off (in GCC, kept until its files are labeled); co-authoring only when every tool that reads labels supports it
If late (decisions): Encrypted files in SharePoint can't be searched, co-authored or scanned, and ring 2 waits

Phase: Phase 2 — Containers, SharePoint and OneDrive, and mail
Name: Label integration on for SharePoint and OneDrive, after labels have replicated to the service

Phase: Phase 2 — Containers, SharePoint and OneDrive, and mail
Name: Legacy IRM libraries moved to sensitivity labels one by one, a volunteer library first; IRM turned off on each

Phase: Phase 2 — Containers, SharePoint and OneDrive, and mail
Name: Container classes and who may create Teams, groups and sites
Options (decisions): A container label per class with its privacy, guest and unmanaged-device settings; creation open to all, or limited to a group, for each class
If late (decisions): Container labels can't be piloted, and the oversharing work Copilot waits for can't start

Phase: Phase 2 — Containers, SharePoint and OneDrive, and mail
Name: Conditional Access baseline enforced; emergency access accounts tested (program P1.6)
If late (decisions): Container labels' unmanaged-device setting has no Conditional Access baseline to work with

Phase: Phase 2 — Containers, SharePoint and OneDrive, and mail
Name: Container labels: pilot sites for two weeks with Conditional Access in report-only, then required for new containers and applied to CUI-bearing sites for two

Phase: Phase 2 — Containers, SharePoint and OneDrive, and mail
Name: Approved message-encryption scenarios, and the recipient experience
Options (decisions): Sender opt-in, named offices, Do Not Forward to a partner, expiring mail where Advanced Message Encryption is licensed; one-time passcodes on or off; social IDs on or off; branding
If late (decisions): Transport rules can't be written, and message encryption waits

Phase: Phase 2 — Containers, SharePoint and OneDrive, and mail
Name: Message encryption verified and branded; each transport rule in Audit for two weeks, enforced for ring 1 for one, then rings 2 and 3

Phase: Phase 2 — Containers, SharePoint and OneDrive, and mail
Name: Gate 2 — Containers, libraries and mail protected
Criteria (gates): Container labels required for new sites and applied to CUI sites, with guest add and unmanaged-device access tested; label integration on and IRM libraries migrated or dated; an encrypted test message opened by an external recipient, with the rule hit in the message trace

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: DLP outcomes for each class and surface: block, warn, or allow with justification
Options (decisions): Outcome statements per class for mail, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive, and Windows devices, each with its exceptions and their expiry
If late (decisions): DLP policies can't be written, and simulation waits

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: Custom sensitive information types written as code; exact data match where the class needs it

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: Workload DLP in simulation for the pilot across a business cycle; matched items exported before the 30 days are up

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: Workload DLP enforced ring by ring: ring 2 with override and justification, ring 3 everyone in scope; false positives tuned

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: Pilot devices moved by pattern (program P2.3)
If late (decisions): Endpoint DLP has no managed pilot devices to onboard

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: Endpoint DLP on Windows: pilot devices onboarded, rules in Audit for two weeks, then enforced ring by ring

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: Service-side auto-labeling in simulation over pilot sites, PDFs in scope; precision recorded; automatic turn-on left off

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: Move each auto-labeling policy from simulation to labeling
Options (decisions): Turn the policy on once its false positives are resolved; keep it in simulation
If late (decisions): Existing content stays unlabeled, and PDF support in SharePoint stays off

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: Auto-labeling policies on; PDF support turned on in SharePoint and OneDrive

Phase: Phase 3 — DLP and auto-labeling
Name: Gate 3 — DLP and auto-labeling enforced
Criteria (gates): Synthetic sensitive content blocked on each surface and the alert received by security operations; every rule exception with an expiry; auto-labeling precision recorded and sample files labeled as designed

Phase: Phase 4 — Insider risk and AI data security
Name: Insider risk charter drafted: purpose and templates, notice and privacy documentation, bargaining obligations, investigator powers, roles, retention

Phase: Phase 4 — Insider risk and AI data security
Name: Adopt the insider risk charter
Owner or approver: CISO, with the senior agency official for privacy and general counsel
Options (decisions): Adopt it, then configure; don't configure Insider Risk Management or Communication Compliance
If late (decisions): Neither tool can be configured, and Gate 4 waits

Phase: Phase 4 — Insider risk and AI data security
Name: Insider Risk Management and Communication Compliance for a pilot scope: a 30-day audit phase, alerts triaged, a tuning record

Phase: Phase 4 — Insider risk and AI data security
Name: AI data decisions: approved AI apps and their data, labels Copilot mustn't process, oversharing remediation, who may read prompts
Options (decisions): Per app class (Copilot in the tenant, enterprise AI apps, third-party AI sites): approve for named classes, or block. Prompt and response access settled with the privacy official and counsel
If late (decisions): AI policies can't leave simulation, and Copilot reaches users before oversharing is fixed

Phase: Phase 4 — Insider risk and AI data security
Name: Data risk assessment for oversharing read; DSPM and Copilot DLP in simulation for at least two weeks across a month-end

Phase: Phase 4 — Insider risk and AI data security
Name: Copilot DLP enforced; paste to unapproved AI sites blocked; a labeled file cited but not summarized

Phase: Phase 4 — Insider risk and AI data security
Name: Gate 4 — Insider risk and AI data governed
Criteria (gates): Charter adopted before configuration; Insider Risk Management and Communication Compliance on for their scope after the audit phase, with users excluded only by the privacy official's approval; Copilot DLP enforced and AI-site paste blocked; approved AI apps and label exclusions recorded

Phase: Phase 5 — Operations and evidence
Name: Configuration baseline exported and reviewed; drift run scheduled; first drift run with no unexplained differences

Phase: Phase 5 — Operations and evidence
Name: Operating cadence written into the day-two runbook; quarterly synthetic tests run once; help desk briefed

Phase: Phase 5 — Operations and evidence
Name: Assessor's package assembled from the evidence catalog; Zero Trust Assessment rerun

Phase: Phase 5 — Operations and evidence
Name: Gate 5 — Operated with evidence
Criteria (gates): Every row of the implementation checklist ticked with the evidence the catalog names; first drift run clean; quarterly synthetic tests passed once; assessor's package assembled (closure is the authorizing official's decision)
